If we plug in $x=0$ we get the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ so  we apply L'Hopital's rule to find the limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{x}^{2}}{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{[{x}^{2}]}^{′}}{[1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{2x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{x}^{2}}{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{2x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{[2x]}^{′}}{{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{2}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)} \\  & =2{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
